label: r1c3
name: attention with wrap-around bias
hypothesis: Inserts one multi-head self-attention layer over all cells after the stem, before the 3x3 trunk. Each head has a learned position bias indexed by row offset and by column offset with wrap-around; the bias starts at zero and is scaled up so it can learn quickly. Heads can learn to attend 3, 4 or 5 columns over, bringing in target features. The recipe matches the second candidate. If it scores clearly below the second candidate, attention learns the shift too slowly for this budget.
last_analysis: Aligning the shifted target is the key: none of 0, wrap-around row conv 0.65, wrap-around attention 0.81. Most of the gap between runs is seed collapse into early DONE, not skill. r2c1 scored 0.87 on one seed and 0 on the other; both seeds of r2c2 collapsed, as did one seed of r3c2. Runs that survive score about 0.75–0.88. Entropy 0.02 did not stop collapse. A second attention block and split stems both slowed learning. Collapse happens because random placements cost reward until the shift is learned. So the most promising levers are (a) learning the alignment faster: attention values taken by a linear map straight from the raw observation, so the shifted target arrives intact, and (b) a standard near-uniform policy start (small output-layer init), so DONE gets no early lead. Last round: test each lever alone on r1c3, plus both together.
